headline_marked: Jamaat-led alliance [[starts Dhaka-Chattogram long march]] for people's rights
headline: Jamaat-led alliance starts Dhaka-Chattogram long march for people's rights
summary: The 11-party alliance, led by Jamaat-e-Islami, has launched a convoy of around 1,500 vehicles to demand an end to utility crises and price hikes.
details: A Jamaat-led 11-party alliance has launched a long march from Dhaka to Chattogram today, starting from Shapla Chattar at 8:30 am after an inaugural rally.

Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman stated that the movement will continue until the rights of the country's 180 million people are established, focusing on issues like gas, electricity, and water crises.
The alliance's six-point demands include the implementation of the referendum verdict, trial of the 2024 July massacre, curbing price hikes of essentials, and ending corruption and extortion.
Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam warned that if the government obstructs the march, the alliance's six-point demand will turn into a single-point demand.
The convoy, consisting of approximately 1,500 vehicles, is scheduled to end at Laldighi Maidan in Chattogram, with several roadside rallies planned along the way.
To minimize public inconvenience, the alliance leaders coordinated with police to ensure the convoy uses only one side of the highway to keep traffic flowing.
Further long marches are planned for Rangpur on September 19, Khulna on October 10, and Sylhet on October 24, concluding with a grand rally in Dhaka on November 14.

headline_marked: 3 decomposed bodies, including a newborn, [[recovered from locked flat in Ashulia]]
headline: 3 decomposed bodies, including a newborn, recovered from locked flat in Ashulia
summary: Police found the remains of an unidentified man, woman, and a newborn in a rented room after neighbors reported a foul smell.
details: Police recovered the decomposed bodies of an unidentified man, a woman, and a newborn from a locked room in the Jamgora area of Ashulia, Savar, early today.
The discovery was made around 2:30 am on the second floor of a four-storey building in Madhya Jamgora after local residents alerted authorities about a foul smell emanating from the room.
According to Mohammad Tariqul Islam, officer-in-charge of Ashulia Police Station, the couple had rented the room a few days prior, introducing themselves as husband and wife.
The woman was reportedly nearly five months pregnant at the time. Police believe the baby may have been delivered after the woman died, as her body had already begun to decompose.
A forensic team from the Criminal Investigation Department visited the scene to collect evidence. Police initially suspect the deaths may be the result of murder.
Authorities are currently working to identify the deceased adults and investigate the circumstances surrounding their deaths.
caption:

Police recovered the decomposed bodies of an unidentified man, a woman, and a newborn from a locked room in the Jamgora area of Ashulia, Savar, early today.

According to Mohammad Tariqul Islam, officer-in-charge of Ashulia Police Station, the couple had rented the room a few days prior, introducing themselves as husband and wife.

The woman was reportedly nearly five months pregnant at the time. Police believe the baby may have been delivered after the woman died, as her body had already begun to decompose.

A forensic team from the Criminal Investigation Department visited the scene to collect evidence. Police initially suspect the deaths may be the result of murder.

Authorities are currently working to identify the deceased adults and investigate the circumstances surrounding their deaths.
